summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the Build My Church series with a message titled Build It on Your Knees. Erica, the online host, opened by inviting everyone to ask what would change if prayer became our first response instead of our last resort. Pastor Travis then shared his longing for a genuine move of God and an encounter with Him, not just a church service. He rooted the message in Jesus' promise in Matthew 16:18 that He will build His church, and in Psalm 127:1, which says that unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain. He shared a story from his teenage years about the power of his mother's prayers, then walked through the book of Acts to show that the early church was built on prayer, not on business plans or strategies.

He offered four truths about prayer. First, prayer goes where we cannot go, reaching people and places beyond our words and our reach, as Paul's request for an open door in Colossians 4:3 shows. Second, powerful prayers are specific. Drawing on Philippians 4:6-7 and 1 Timothy 2:1, he encouraged believers to move beyond general requests and to intercede for others by name. Third, there is strength in praying together. Pastor Travis explained that the Greek word for agree in Matthew 18:19-20 is the root of our word symphony, picturing believers in harmony, and he compared it to two flames making a bigger fire. Fourth, prayer carries eternal weight. He spoke with urgency and a pastor's burden about the reality of eternity and the need to care deeply about those who do not yet know Jesus.

For application, everyone was invited to write the names of people who need Jesus on the Build My Church prayer card and to keep it somewhere visible to pray over daily. He announced an urgent prayer gathering with anointing on Wednesday at 7:00 p.m. He also announced an Invite a Friend Sunday in two weeks, encouraging everyone to invite someone, and he cited a poll in which 96% of non-churchgoers said they would attend if a friend invited them. He then invited anyone wanting to follow Jesus to come forward, and he led a prayer of confession and thanksgiving. Erica closed by encouraging us to pray before we react or decide, to make prayer intentional for family, church, and neighbors, and to see giving as an act of trust in God.
mainPoints: Everything God builds, including His church, is built on prayer, and prayer reaches people and places we cannot reach ourselves.
Powerful prayer is specific and intercessory: put a name on it, keep praying for those who need Jesus, and do not give up when you see no change yet.
Praying together in agreement multiplies our faith, and the reality of eternity should move us to pray and invite others to know Jesus.

versesMentioned.text: He must become greater; I must become less.
And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.
Then he fell on his knees and cried out, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep.
So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain. Unless the Lord watches over the city, the guards stand watch in vain.
And pray for us, too, that God may open a door for our message, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
For even his own brothers did not believe in him.

Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
I urge, then, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercession and thanksgiving be made for all people.
Again, truly I tell you that if two of you on earth agree about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven. For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.
But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile.

Monday.scripture: Psalm 127:1 (NIV): "Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain."
Monday.focus: Building your day, your work, and your home on prayer before your own plans.
Monday.action: Before checking your phone or email this morning, spend five minutes on your knees or in a quiet spot asking God to lead everything you are building.
Monday.prayer: Lord, You are the builder. Before I plan or act, I come to You. Align my heart with Yours and lead my steps this week. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Philippians 4:6-7 (NIV): "Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God."
Tuesday.focus: Praying specifically instead of in general terms.
Tuesday.action: Write down three specific requests you have been praying about in general terms, then pray over each one by name or detail and add a line of thanksgiving.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I bring my specific needs to You today. Thank You for hearing me. Guard my heart and mind with Your peace. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 18:19-20 (NIV): "For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them."
Wednesday.focus: The strength of praying together in agreement.
Wednesday.action: Ask a family member, friend, or small group member to pray with you today, in person or by phone. If you are able, join the Wednesday evening prayer gathering at church.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, thank You for being present when we gather in Your name. Teach us to agree together in prayer and to carry one another's burdens. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 1 Timothy 2:1 (NIV): "I urge, then, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercession and thanksgiving be made for all people."
Thursday.focus: Interceding by name for people who need Jesus.
Thursday.action: Write names on your Build My Church prayer card, or on a piece of paper if you do not have one. Place it where you will see it daily and pray for each person by name.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, I lift up these names to You. Draw each person to Yourself, soften hearts, and give me patience to keep praying and not give up. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Colossians 4:3 (NIV): "And pray for us, too, that God may open a door for our message."
Friday.focus: Trusting that prayer goes where we cannot go.
Friday.action: Think of someone you cannot easily reach or change. Pray for an open door in their life, and send them a short, kind message of encouragement.
Friday.prayer: God, my words cannot reach every place, but You can. Open doors for the gospel and work in hearts I cannot touch. I trust You. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Matthew 28:19 (NIV): "Therefore go and make disciples of all nations."
Saturday.focus: Praying and preparing to invite someone to church.
Saturday.action: Choose one person from your prayer list and decide how you will invite them to church or to coffee. Pray for them first, then send the invitation if you feel ready.
Saturday.prayer: Jesus, give me courage and compassion to invite others. Prepare their hearts and use me to point them to You. Amen.

title: How to Pray for Someone Who Won't Change | Build It on Your Knees
